failure_modes: Treating a process as irreducible because no shortcut has been found yet
Assuming a reducible higher level exists because one exists for similar-looking systems
Knowing the structure mistaken for knowing the dynamics, as with a connectome that maps wiring but not firing
gloss: Some processes have no shortcut: the only way to know step n is to run n steps
invariants: Irreducibility holds even when the rules are fully known and deterministic
Any exact predictor of an irreducible process takes at least as many steps as the process
mechanism: For a computationally irreducible process, no procedure predicts its state at step n in fewer steps than the process itself takes. Simple rules can generate such behaviour, as the cellular automaton Rule 110 shows. Reducible processes are the exception: their low-level mechanics produce higher-level regularities, like billiard balls, that a shorter description can capture.
